message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 234, "amount_cents": 4004}, {"order_id": 235, "amount_cents": 1660}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll check the refund records.

The ledger's refund records match Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 234 and 235, same amounts). Next I'll check the orders list to confirm the refunds correspond to real orders before relying on net_balance.

Both refunds match real orders (234 belongs to birch, 235 to cobalt) and the amounts are within the order totals, so I see no reason to hold. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 36083, which matches its orders (18974 + 17109 = 36083) with no refunds. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which should reflect the 4004 refund on order 234.
Birch's net of 28695 matches its orders (21055 + 11644 = 32699) minus the 4004 refund on order 234. Next I'll check cobalt, which should reflect the 1660 refund on order 235.
All three net balances match the orders minus the refunds (cobalt: 14171 + 16756 - 1660 = 29267), so Alpha's refund work checks out and there's no reason to hold. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout is recorded and Alpha's refunds checked out against the ledger, so I'll record birch's payout of 28695, its net balance.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's net balance of 29267 was already checked against its orders minus the 1660 refund. Alpha's refunds are verified, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully after verifying Alpha's refunds against the ledger and orders. Acme 36083, birch 28695, cobalt 29267. Finishing with the report.
